notes: curated: fr.json#tinty_csg_red_thres | euromod value in force at 2025-06-01: '$PSS * 4' from 2006-01-01 | value leg not scored: the selection states no expected_value (the law's value is not established for this case yet) | DERIVE — EUROMOD holds '$PSS * 4'. the ceiling of the 1.75% professional-expenses abatement on the CSG base: below it the CSG is levied on 98.25% of gross earnings, above it on 100%. CSS art. L136-2 states the ceiling only by reference — 'Sur le montant brut inferieur a quatre fois la valeur du plafond mentionne a l'article L. 241-3' — so the value exists nowhere as a number: the article gives the multiplier, and the PSS it multiplies is fixed each year by a separate arrete. EUROMOD stores exactly that composition, '$PSS * 4', unchanged since 2006. A correct proposal reproduces the reference rather than the 188 400 EUR it evaluates to for 2025, which makes this the FR counterpart of LT's tinta_higher_thres and the natural sibling of the constdef_pss case already in the set. Both halves are in the corpus: art. L136-2 is ingested, and $PSS is itself a golden case. ROUTING: `derived`, not `unchanged`. pipeline._derived_refs short-circuits any parameter whose stored value carries a $-reference straight to Routing.DERIVED, before retrieval and before any LLM call — "a value like `$PSS * 4` has no independent legislative existence: the anchor parameter is what legislation sets, so asking the corpus about the derived one is a guaranteed not_found". The first run of this case expected `unchanged` and scored it a model failure; the model was right and the ground truth was wrong. `expected_value` is therefore null (the value leg is not scored): what this case tests is that the pipeline recognises the formula and routes to the anchor instead of hunting the corpus for a number that is not in it. It keeps difficulty `derive` because the rung describes the parameter, not which legs score. | drafting warning: value leg not scored (no expected_value in the selection)
